cases.refreshed: ¿Estás cansado de no poder hacer cosas tecnológicas por ti mismo? ¿Cansado de esperar a que los miembros de tu familia te ayuden o hagan las cosas por ti? ¡Ahora puedes aprender a hacer todo eso por ti mismo! Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarte a un punto de acceso o a una red Wi-Fi; Usar Chromebooks o computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar clases de la biblioteca e inscribirte en ellas; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Usar un teléfono móvil; Buscar en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estará allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puedes asistir a tu cita, llama para cancelarla. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere inscripción. Para inscribirte, llama al (408) 294-1237.

cases.refreshed: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
